name: Club
credit: Virtuosity Drums — Versilian Studios and Karoryfer Samples, performed by Austin McMahon
_what: Austin McMahon's kit at Virtuosity in Boston, recorded the way a live
club date is recorded. Six mic positions; this recipe uses four of them.
`lofi` is the vintage mic and is a colour, not a kit — left out. `perc`
is the VSCO percussion and is not a drum kit voice.
swap_stereo is on because the overheads are imaged from in front of the
kit: measured on the source, the hat sits 3.3 dB right and the ride
3.9 dB left. The brief wants the drummer's seat, and one honest channel
swap on the stereo mics turns the whole kit round at once — hat left,
ride right, high tom left of low tom — without inventing a pan that the
room never had. The mono close mics stay centred, which is where a kick
and a snare belong either way.
No `pan` is written into kit.json for this kit: the stereo image is in
the files, because it is the real one the overheads captured. The
manifest's pan field is for kits whose voices arrive mono.
_spacing: 4.5 dB is the default step between layers and it is what the cymbals
get, because the library gives them three or four dynamics and that is
the whole range there is. The snare, the toms and the cross-stick are
sampled 16 to 36 dynamics deep over 30-odd dB, and 4.5 dB steps spend
all four layers inside the top third of that — four flavours of a
backbeat and no ghost note. They get 8 dB, which puts layer 1 on a
_balance: dB relative to the snare's accent layer, as K-weighted loudness over the
first 400 ms — how loud each drum seems when it is struck. These are the
numbers to argue with when the owner says 'less hat'; the render tool
measures what it got and writes the difference into trim_db, so the
files never change when the balance does.
_mix: close 1.0, overheads 0.7, room 0.35 is the brief's live-recording
default and it is what the drums use. The cymbals and toms have no close
mic in this library, so the overheads become the close mic at 1.0 and
`mid` — the mid-distance pair — supplies the proximity the overheads
lack. Every mic is time-aligned onto the heaviest-weighted one before
it is summed; the room arrives 6-10 ms late on this kit.
